from.name: Radia Perlman distributed spanning-tree bridge design

property: Distributed root selection and computation of a loop-free spanning subset of a redundantly connected extended LAN become part of the standardized bridge loop-control lineage.

date_or_range.notes: The 1985 paper documents the distributed spanning-tree bridge algorithm; RFC 1493 later documents the IEEE 802.1D-1990 bridge/STP operational model.

sources.supports: distributed spanning-tree bridge design, root/path computation and loop-free active topology

sources.locator: RFC 1493, IEEE 802.1D-1990 bridge/STP objects and dot1dStpProtocolSpecification
sources.supports: operational existence of an IEEE 802.1D spanning-tree lineage and its distinction from DEC LANbridge 100 STP
sources.notes: The exact DEC/IEEE committee revision path still requires primary standards/implementation records.

negative_claims: This edge does not claim that the 1985 paper is byte-for-byte identical to the IEEE 802.1D-1990 protocol specification.
This edge does not collapse DEC LANbridge 100 STP and IEEE 802.1D STP into one wire protocol.
This edge does not establish the exact date at which each algorithmic detail entered the IEEE standard.
open_questions: Acquire DEC bridge manuals and protocol descriptions preceding IEEE 802.1D-1990.
Recover IEEE 802.1 committee history showing the transition from DEC implementation/design work to standardized STP.
Build PDU, timer and state-machine diffs between DEC LANbridge 100 STP and IEEE 802.1D editions.
Trace later RSTP and MSTP revisions as separate formal descendants.
notes: A design-influence edge intentionally weaker than revision-of: algorithmic ancestry is documented, but exact standards wording and wire-format genealogy must be reconstructed separately.
